> Terry told Martin that he would terribly lose the election.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **Terry told Martin, “You will lose the election terribly.”** / **Terry told Martin, “I will lose the election terribly.”**
>
> _He_ could refer to Terry or Martin; direct speech removes the doubt. (The adverb also belongs after the object: _lose the election terribly_.)
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

**Ambiguous pronoun reference** occurs when a pronoun (_he, she, it, they_) could refer to **more than one antecedent**. Fix it by repeating the noun or rephrasing (often with direct speech). _He_ could refer to Terry or Martin; direct speech removes the doubt. (The adverb also belongs after the object: _lose the election terribly_.)

## Simplified explanation

Use **direct speech** to show who will lose.

body: Write a **five-paragraph essay** (about 500 words) on: **How to minimise conflict in elections in Ghana.**
answer:
> [!answer]
> **Model plan (five-paragraph essay):**
>
> 1. **Introduction:** Elections are central to Ghana's democracy, but they are often marred by tension, violence and disputes (e.g. clashes at polling stations, vigilante groups). **Thesis:** conflict can be minimised through a credible electoral process, responsible political conduct and effective civic education.
> 2. **Body 1: A credible and transparent process.** An independent, well-resourced Electoral Commission; a clean biometric register; transparent collation with party agents; prompt, accurate announcement of results; credible avenues for disputes (the courts).
> 3. **Body 2: Responsible conduct of politicians and the security services.** Disbanding party vigilante groups (Vigilantism Act, 2019); avoiding inflammatory language; peace pacts brokered by the National Peace Council; neutral and professional policing.
> 4. **Body 3: Civic education and the role of the media and civil society.** The NCCE educating citizens on tolerance; balanced media reporting and an end to hate speech; observer groups (CODEO); the involvement of religious and traditional leaders.
> 5. **Conclusion:** Restate the thesis; peaceful elections are a shared responsibility; a call to action for every Ghanaian.
>
> **Marking focus:** a clear thesis; one main idea per paragraph with a **topic sentence**, support and examples; coherence and transitions (_first, furthermore, finally_); correct grammar, spelling and punctuation; about 500 words.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The five-paragraph essay: an **introduction** (hook, background, thesis), **three body paragraphs** (topic sentence, supporting details, examples, a concluding or transitional sentence) and a **conclusion** (restated thesis, summary, final thought). Coherence comes from logical order and transitions; unity from keeping every sentence on the paragraph's topic.

## Simplified explanation

hint: Thesis in the introduction; one solution per body paragraph.

> 2. **Body 1: Infrastructure and waste management.** Adequate public and household toilets; regular refuse collection, more bins and skips; recycling of plastics; proper drainage; private-sector participation (e.g. waste-management companies).

body: Write a **five-paragraph essay** (about 500 words): **Argue for or against the view that student demonstrations should be banned.**
answer:
> [!answer]
> **Model plan (against a ban):**
>
> 1. **Introduction:** Student demonstrations have sometimes turned violent (destruction of property, closure of universities). **Thesis:** demonstrations should not be banned but properly regulated, because they are a constitutional right, a channel for legitimate grievances, and a check on authorities.
> 2. **Body 1: A democratic right.** The 1992 Constitution (Article 21) guarantees freedom of assembly; a ban would be unconstitutional and authoritarian.
> 3. **Body 2: An outlet for grievances.** Demonstrations draw attention to genuine problems (fees, accommodation, poor facilities) that authorities may ignore; they encourage dialogue and reform.
> 4. **Body 3: Regulation instead of prohibition.** Notifying the police under the Public Order Act; peaceful conduct; dialogue mechanisms (SRC–management meetings); sanctions for violent individuals rather than a blanket ban.
> 5. **Conclusion:** A ban treats the symptom, not the cause; responsible, regulated protest strengthens university governance and democracy.
>
> _(A candidate may argue **for** a ban, citing violence, destruction of property, disruption of academic calendars and the availability of alternative channels such as dialogue, as long as the argument is consistent and well supported.)_

In an **argumentative essay**, the thesis takes a clear position; each body paragraph presents one reason with evidence; a **counter-argument and rebuttal** strengthens the case; the conclusion reaffirms the position.
